Loading data from preprocessing step

data <- read.csv("cleaned_data.csv", sep = ",")

Visualize the curves, splitted by type of day

unique(data$day_cat)
## [1] "WDSH" "SA"   "SASH" "SUPH" "WD"
  • WD: Working day (outside of school holidays periods)
  • WDSH: Working day during school holidays
  • SA: Saturday (outside of school holidays periods)
  • SASH: Saturday during school holidays
  • SUPH: Sunday and bank holidays
plot_curves <- function(data_to_plot) {
  ggplot(data_to_plot, aes(
    x = time_slot,
    y = percentage_entering,
    group = station_id
  )) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
    facet_wrap(~day_cat) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
    theme_minimal()
}

data_WDSH <- data %>%
  filter(day_cat == 'WDSH')
data_SA <- data %>%
  filter(day_cat == 'SA')
data_SASH <- data %>%
  filter(day_cat == 'SASH')
data_SUPH <- data %>%
  filter(day_cat == 'SUPH')
data_WD <- data %>%
  filter(day_cat == 'WD')

plot_curves(data_WD)

plot_curves(data_WDSH)

plot_curves(data_SA)

plot_curves(data_SASH)

plot_curves(data_SUPH)

Definition of function for computing bicluster properties

See Definition 2.1 in the FunCC paper.

In this implementation, we consider:

  • I: set of stations
  • J: set of day types i.e. j (WDSH,SA,SASH,SUPH,WD)

each f_ij = f_ij(time_slot).

The properties of a bicluster will be its mean, the alpha_i and the beta_j functional curves.

We decided to mimic the setting shown in Definition 2.1 thoroughly, also creating a “cube” representing the bicluster (indexed by [i,j,t]) in order to make the functions general purpose and more reusable.

create_bicluster <- function(data, row_var, col_var, time_var, value_var){
  
  I_set = sort(unique(data[[row_var]]))
  J_set = sort(unique(data[[col_var]]))

  card_I = length(I_set)
  card_J = length(J_set)
  
  n_slots = length(unique(data[[time_var]]))
  slots = seq_len(n_slots) -1

  bicluster = array(0, dim = c(card_I, card_J, n_slots),
                dimnames = list(I_set, J_set, slots))

  for (r in seq_len(nrow(data))) {
    i = match(data[[row_var]][r], I_set)
    j = match(data[[col_var]][r], J_set)
    t = data[[time_var]][r] + 1
    bicluster[i, j, t] = data[[value_var]][r]
  }
  return(bicluster)
}

Also in this case we thoroughly followed the equations shown in Definition 2.1

compute_bicluster_properties <- function(bicluster) {
  I_set <- dimnames(bicluster)[[1]]
  J_set <- dimnames(bicluster)[[2]]
  slots <- dimnames(bicluster)[[3]]

  card_I  <- dim(bicluster)[1]
  card_J  <- dim(bicluster)[2]
  n_slots <- dim(bicluster)[3]

  mu_IJ <- numeric(n_slots)

  for (t in seq_len(n_slots)) {
    for (i in 1:card_I) {
      for (j in 1:card_J) {
        mu_IJ[t] = mu_IJ[t] + bicluster[i, j, t]
      }
    }
    mu_IJ[t] = mu_IJ[t] / (card_I * card_J)
  }

  alpha_IJ = matrix(0, nrow = card_I, ncol = n_slots, dimnames = list(I_set, slots))

  for (t in seq_len(n_slots)) {
    for (i in 1:card_I) {
      for (j in 1:card_J) {
        alpha_IJ[i, t] = alpha_IJ[i, t] + bicluster[i, j, t]
      }
      alpha_IJ[i, t] = alpha_IJ[i, t] / card_J - mu_IJ[t]
    }
  }

  beta_IJ <- matrix(0, nrow = card_J, ncol = n_slots, dimnames = list(J_set, slots))


  for (t in seq_len(n_slots)) {
    for (j in 1:card_J) {
      for (i in 1:card_I) {
        beta_IJ[j, t] = beta_IJ[j, t] + bicluster[i, j, t]
      }
      beta_IJ[j, t] = beta_IJ[j, t] / card_I - mu_IJ[t]
    }
  }

  return(list(mu_IJ = mu_IJ, alpha_IJ = alpha_IJ, beta_IJ = beta_IJ))
}

Check on global set

whole_dataset_bicluster <- create_bicluster(data, 'station_id', 'day_cat', 'time_slot', 'percentage_entering')
res <- compute_bicluster_properties(whole_dataset_bicluster)

mu_IJ    <- res$mu_IJ
alpha_IJ <- res$alpha_IJ
beta_IJ  <- res$beta_IJ

Global mean mu

ggplot(data, aes(
  x = time_slot,
  y = percentage_entering,
  group = station_id
)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(
    data = data.frame(
      time_slot = 0:23,
      mu_IJ = mu_IJ
    ),
    aes(x = time_slot, y = mu_IJ),
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 1.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  theme_minimal()

alpha: Station effect

alpha_df <- as.data.frame(alpha_IJ) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("station_id") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -station_id,
    names_to = "time_slot",
    values_to = "alpha"
  ) |>
  mutate(time_slot = as.numeric(time_slot))

ggplot(alpha_df, aes(
  x = time_slot,
  y = alpha,
  group = station_id
)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  labs(
    title = "Station effects (alpha)",
    x = "Time slot",
    y = "Alpha"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

beta: day category effects

beta_df <- as.data.frame(beta_IJ) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("day_cat") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -day_cat,
    names_to = "time_slot",
    values_to = "beta"
  ) |>
  mutate(time_slot = as.numeric(time_slot))

ggplot(beta_df, aes(
  x = time_slot,
  y = beta,
  color = day_cat,
  group = day_cat
)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  labs(
    title = "Day category effects (beta)",
    x = "Time slot",
    y = "Beta",
    color = "Day category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Example: beta_SUPH + mu overlayed on SUPH curves

beta_mu_df <- data.frame(
  time_slot = 0:23,
  profile = as.numeric(beta_IJ["SUPH", ] + mu_IJ),
  day_cat = "SUPH"
)

ggplot(data_SUPH, aes(
  x = time_slot,
  y = percentage_entering,
  group = station_id
)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15, color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(
    data = beta_mu_df,
    aes(x = time_slot, y = profile, color = day_cat),
    linewidth = 1.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  labs(
    title = "SUPH: observed curves vs reconstructed profile",
    x = "Time slot",
    y = "Percentage entering",
    color = "Day category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Implement H-score function

(As in Definition 2.2 of the paper)

compute_h_score <- function(bicluster, mu_IJ, alpha_IJ, beta_IJ){

  slots <- dimnames(bicluster)[[3]]

  card_I  <- dim(bicluster)[1]
  card_J  <- dim(bicluster)[2]
  n_slots <- dim(bicluster)[3]
  
  H = 0
  for (i in 1:card_I){
    for(j in 1:card_J){
      
      # compute the L2 norm, that in our case is a discrete integral
      for(t in seq_len(n_slots)){
        # \bar f_ij(t) = \mu(t) + \alpha_i(t) + \beta_j(t)
        H = H+(bicluster[i,j,t]-(mu_IJ[t]+alpha_IJ[i,t]+beta_IJ[j,t]))^2
      }
    }
  }
  H = H/(card_I*card_J)
  return(H)
}

Check in the whole dataset

compute_h_score(whole_dataset_bicluster, mu_IJ, alpha_IJ, beta_IJ)
## [1] 54.18675
